title: Clarinet models in New Orleans and the music's migration north
summary: He copied Jimmie Noone, Big Eye Louis and teacher Lorenzo Tio; New Orleans music spread via Chicago to New York.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Who were some of the people that you were copying at the time? Who, me? Yeah.

I copied anybody I could. Anybody? I used to, I loved Jimmy Noon, and I loved Big I, Louis, and of course I loved my teacher Lorenzo Teo, and I loved Alphonse Piku, and they were about the best, as far as the clarinet is concerned, they were about the best down there.
This was really the experimental, the pioneering stage of music, wasn't it, where no one had been, shall we say, moving in the direction of this kind of music, and these were fellas that were-

No, no, it was a different kind of music altogether. I mean, the people, the guys up north, they didn't, they've never heard anything like that until the musicians from Noon began to migrate, and they went to Chicago, it was the first stop. And then, move on into New York, and things began to happen, and they began to appreciate it.
